summary: Hermann Schlagintweit studied at the University of Munich (~1845–1849) and held a post at the University of Berlin (~1851–1854).

Active in religious studies, linguistics, and philosophy, Hermann Usener studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and Bonn between ~1853 and ~1858. He held posts at the universities of Bern (~1861–1863), Greifswald (~1863–1866), and Bonn (~1866–1905), teaching Hermann Osthoff and Friedrich Leo.

Linguist Hermann Wilhelm Ebel studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, August Boeckh, and August Friedrich Pott. He taught at Beheim-Schwarzbach'sche Realschule and Gymnasium Schneidemühl before chairing comparative philology at Berlin (1872).

Active in linguistics and philosophy, Heymann Steinthal studied at the University of Berlin under August Boeckh (~1843–1847). He later taught Berthold Delbrück and Wilhelm Radloff while holding posts at the University of Berlin (~1850–1899) and Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura, a Buddhist studies scholar, completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also held a post as a researcher attested in 1995.

Hideaki Nakatani, working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, studied at Kyoto University and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Gadjin M. Nagao and Yutaka Ochihara. He taught Jonathan A. Silk and was a professor at Kobe Gakuin University (attested 2003).
Hidehiko Kurita specializes in religious studies and Japanology. He earned a PhD from Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University (attested 2020).
Hideki Kiyoshima, working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studied at the University of Delhi and served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).

Hideki Yukawa studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and Osaka University (~1934–1938). He held academic posts at Osaka University (~1933–1939), Kyoto University (~1939–1970), the University of Tokyo (~1939–1950), and Columbia University (~1949–1953).
Historian, archaeologist, and Sinologist Hidemasa Nagata studied at Kyoto University from ~1952 to ~1960 and later served on its faculty from ~1969 to ~1996.

Linguist Hidenaka Tanaka studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, the University of Oxford, and Kyoto University. He taught Yutaka Iwamoto and held positions at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University (1920, 1931–1946), and Kyoto Women's University (~1947–1974).

Active in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Hidenori Kitagawa was a Rockefeller Foundation fellow (1952–1953) and professor at Nagoya University (attested 1968–1969). He taught Musashi Tachikawa and Takanori Unno.

Scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology Hidenori Sakuma studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. His posts include International Buddhist University, Otani University, University of Tsukuba, and Taisho University.

Hideo Mineshima, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at Taisho and Waseda universities. He held long-term posts at Waseda University (1960–1998) and Bunkyo Gakuin University, and headed several scholarly organizations including the Japanese Association for Comparative Philosophy.
Buddhist studies scholar Hideo Sakurai studied at Tohoku University (~1940–1943) and served as a professor emeritus at Komazawa University, where he held a post from ~1950 to ~1987.

Active in Indology and Buddhist studies, Hideomi Yaita completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He held positions at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1991–1995) and as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995).
Religious studies scholar Hidetaka Fukazawa studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1974–1979) and held a post at Hitotsubashi University (~1993).
Hideto Ono, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, studied at Komazawa University (~1963–1967) and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (~1983–1992).

Buddhist studies scholar Hidetomo Yoshizawa held several appointments at Taisho University, serving as a researcher (attested 1998), student researcher (attested 2006), lecturer (attested 2008), and chief research fellow (attested 2017).

Hidetsugu Yagi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909) and taught Arthur Waley. He held posts at Tohoku University (~1919–1932), Osaka University (~1932–1946), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1942–1944), and the University of Tokyo (~1944–1945).
